population.note: FICTIONAL. Adults ≈276M. Current users are 37.5% (≈103.5M) and ever-users 50.0% (≈138M), so 12.5% (≈34.5M) used and are off now. About 135M adults have never used. Cycling: about 19.5 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and about 6 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so (19.5 + 6)/50 = 51%. That fits ~35% one-year persistence with 36–47% restarting within a year, made easier by the pill. Ever-use rose 10 pts (limit 12) and current use rose 9.0. Age bands: 18–29: 22% × 52M = 11.4M; 30–49: 42% × 92M = 38.6M; 50–64: 54% × 62M = 33.5M; 65+: 28.5% × 70M = 20.0M. Total ≈103.5M = 37.5%. Income thirds: (40 + 38 + 34.5)/3 = 37.5. The bottom third rose most, by 10 pts, through three routes: $149–150 oral starters, oral-first employer plans, and the gray telehealth and parcel trade (≈10.6M users, up from 7.1M). The top third rose least because it was already high. Growth among 18–29s comes mostly from the pill and from 'peptide clinic' telehealth. The 65+ band rose more slowly because about one in five older ever-users is on a bone pause, a post-NAION stop or a GI-related stop. Never-users cluster in four groups: under-30s, rural residents of non-expansion states, people with contraindications, and a refuser bloc that the Whole Table movement has made visible. Pediatric use is 1.6% of ≈73M ≈ 1.17M, mostly adolescents 12+. The 2035 partial adolescent bone readout showed a small BMD-accrual lag, but no label change followed and the debate continues. About one child in two now lives with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it, and in many households a parent takes 'weekend off' holidays.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Statute unchanged: the Part D obesity benefit pays a $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 copay and a counselling visit, with eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 plus one comorbidity. Medicare pays 18.3% of fills, ≈18.9M users (≈17.4M aged 65+ and ≈1.5M disabled under-65): ≈7.6M for diabetes and ≈11.3M for obesity. Obesity-benefit gross: 11.3M × $199 × 12 ≈ $27.0B. Beneficiary copays: 11.3M × $50 × 12 ≈ $6.8B, leaving ≈$20.2B for the programme. All Medicare incretin fills: 18.9M × $199 × 12 ≈ $45.1B. Medicaid: the same 31 states plus DC use the 90% match and the continuation standard, and none joined or left. Medicaid pays 13.5% of fills: ≈14.0M users × $199 × 12 ≈ $33.4B gross before supplemental rebates. Most new public enrolment is on the 50 mg pill, which is on formularies at the same statutory rate.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 120+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, including generic 50 mg oral semaglutide, plus a growing domestic tirzepatide-copy market. The Telangana first-filer plant is still under US import alert and still supplies India. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide, 'research-grade' retatrutide, and now survodutide and amycretin peptide sold as 'research' material. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 45–75. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics, and Mexican border pharmacies sell generic oral semaglutide over the counter in practice.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices have stalled. Portal and list prices have not moved since the 2033 rise. Injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide cost $249–329; the Wegovy pill 50 mg $299 direct; oral starters (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) $149–150; retatrutide $449 direct and $1,649 list; amycretin $499; MariTide $549 month-equivalent. PBM net is ≈$195–215. The mid-2035 contingent generic date passed with no launch. Payer mix of ≈103.5M users: commercial 36.7% (38.0M); Medicare 18.3% (18.9M); Medicaid 13.5% (14.0M); cash/direct 21.3% (22.0M, including ≈4.1M 'calm'/'focus' subscribers and ≈9M on $149–150 starter doses held long-term); gray/imported/counterfeit 10.2% (10.6M). Sum = 103.5M. The gray 10.6M breaks down as ≈5.2M imported pens, ≈2.4M offshore-compounded telehealth 'peptide clinic' product, ≈1.6M 'research' vials and ≈1.4M counterfeit tablets. About 90% of covering employers gate coverage, about half of those add tenure gates, and most now require oral-first step therapy (the 50 mg pill or Foundayo for 6 months before an injectable). Routes: ≈55% of users take daily orals, up from 36%. Top-efficacy regimens (retatrutide, tirzepatide, MariTide) remain injectable. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand on paper, and the gray clinics operate around them through offshore dispensing.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. 7.2 mg)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance dose)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GIPR-antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscriptions (≈4.1M, down from 4.6M as 'the grey' became a complaint)
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS trial still enrolling)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gray-market 'research' retatrutide, survodutide and amycretin among gym, physique and 'peptide clinic' users
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
planned 'dose holidays' around holidays, weddings and weekends, switching between Foundayo and the Wegovy pill
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new indication and no new molecule approved this step. Oral parity is realised by an existing product: the 50 mg Wegovy pill, approved Feb 2034 at parity with injectable semaglutide, became the most-used incretin form in the US once PBMs adopted oral-first step therapy in 2035. About 55% of users now take daily orals. The pill matches 2.4 mg semaglutide, not tirzepatide or retatrutide. Lilly filed its next-generation oral in Jun 2036, so approval cannot come before mid-2037. FDA issued a complete response letter on the survodutide MASH sNDA in Jul 2035 asking for outcomes data. Bimagrumab-semaglutide was filed in Feb 2036 and is under review with no decision. The SHAPS smoking trial is still enrolling. US market ≈92.9M paying users (103.5M − 10.6M gray) × ≈$195 average net × 12 ≈ $217B. Ex-US ≈$22B and eroding, for a total of ≈$239B. Both manufacturers now disclose product-liability reserves for the GI MDL.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. The shift to the 50 mg pill brings more early nausea. Holiday restarts are adding a spike of acute vomiting.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction: mass-tort litigation
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Ileus is already labelled. Whether the drug causes persistent gastroparesis after stopping is disputed: pooled claims analyses show raised rates of gastric-emptying studies and gastroparesis diagnoses among users, confounded by diabetes. With ≈103.5M users, even rare persistent cases number in the tens of thousands. The federal MDL plus state consolidated proceedings exceed ≈70,000 filed claims. The first bellwether (Oct 2035) returned a $4.2M plaintiff verdict on a failure-to-warn theory; the second (Mar 2036) was a defence verdict.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new FDA action beyond existing labelling. Anaesthesia societies' pre-procedure hold guidance is unchanged. Manufacturers disclose reserves, and settlement talks are reported but not concluded.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Pancreatic cancer claims were folded into the GI MDL docket in 2035, and the court's science-day ruling on general causation is pending. Counterfeit and overdosed gray product confounds reporting.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; litigation is now mass-tort scale; no label change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈2.1M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria in Medicare claims, up from 1.6M. In untrained users over 50, lean mass is 30–40% of the weight lost.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label; body-composition monitoring in high-efficacy labels; CMS annual DEXA requirement for long-term 65+ users unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈9.5M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 9.5M × ~0.6%/yr × 0.35 excess ≈ 20,000 excess hip fractures a year, against ~310,000 US total. The vertebral tail among cycling women aged 50–64 persists. DEXA waits are 8–14 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained; bone endpoints required in filings; CMS 90-day bone-pause code unchanged; DOJ civil case against Novo unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: RR ≈1.7. At ~4/100,000 baseline across ≈103.5M users, that is ≈2,900 excess cases a year, mostly partial and permanent loss of vision in one eye.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions since May 2034; NAION MDL consolidated; no boxed warning.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The 12 mg retatrutide figures stand at ~12% versus ~5% of comparators. A 2035 observational cohort of low-dose oral users (n≈38,000, propensity-matched) found ~7% versus ~5% scoring clinically meaningful anhedonia. It remains unrandomised and confounded by depression on stopping. Self-reported 'grey' is now a common reason given for holidays.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FTC consent orders stand: no 'anxiety treatment' claims. No label change, and no FDA-requested RCT at low dose.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Gating, tenure gaps, bone pauses and GI-litigation-motivated stops all feed it. Pill availability shortens off-periods for the insured.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code; the Seventh Circuit still has not ruled on the Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Common in high-loss older users and among gray-market and peptide-clinic users with no lab monitoring.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Part D counselling screens for it; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of follow-up. The 2035 partial adolescent readout shows a small lag in BMD accrual whose clinical meaning is unclear. Full data slipped to 2037 for one sponsor. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements continue; second extension granted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈10.6M gray users. Poison-centre GLP-1 calls are up a further ~35% on 2034. No cluster this window matched Nov 2033 in size, but there were repeated smaller abscess and sepsis clusters in Florida and Texas linked to offshore 'peptide clinic' vials.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Routine FDA warning letters to telehealth fronts and import alerts; Safe Pens bill still stalled; individuals not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from emerging. ≈1.4M users of pressed tablets; seized lots contain 0–300% of label. GI events and hypoglycaemia in insulin users dominate.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warnings; NABP verified-pharmacy guidance; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg and in gray 'research' users dosing above label.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use; NAION monocular loss is cited as a cofactor in a minority.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Holiday-and-restart patterns are too short to show it, so the burden remains in over-50s with months-long gating or tenure gaps.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint society guidance published 2035; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Several-bpm rise at 12 mg retatrutide; larger and unquantified in gray users stacking 'research' peptides.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Precautionary label; CV outcomes trial ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Restart-at-full-dose GI events after drug holidays
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. With ~30% of users taking at least one planned holiday a year, ED visits for vomiting, dehydration and suspected ileus after restarting a maintenance dose without re-titration rose sharply. They appear in many MDL plaintiff histories.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labels already say to re-titrate after missed doses. Pharmacist counselling guidance updated; no FDA action.

food_and_beverage.state: With 37.5% of adults on the drug, salty snacks fall ~4–5% a year and confectionery ~5–6%. Packaged-food makers sell 'holiday packs' timed to dose-off weekends and Thanksgiving. A small heritage-food bump comes from Whole Table congregations and Southern regional brands, a few points of growth on a small base. Protein lines are split by price tier: premium for the coached, value shakes for the cycling.

alcohol.state: Ninth straight year of spirits volume decline, and beer is down too. Weekend 'holiday' drinking is concentrated, so on-premise sales are spikier and off-premise is flat-to-down. Non-alcoholic formats hold.

restaurants.state: Weekday spend per cover is down ~12% from 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. Friday–Saturday 'holiday night' covers are strong enough that chains staff around them. Memphis and Houston soul-food and buffet rooms gain from Whole Table Sunday traffic. Gram-priced bowls are standard elsewhere.

apparel.state: The 'structured' versus 'cycle' split is now industry-wide. Whole Table and fat-liberation brands revive plus-size fashion in Atlanta and Portland, a small but visible counter-segment. Resale grows.

fitness.state: Still growing. DEXA-plus-coaching chains and Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting' expand, and there is a shortage of trainers qualified for older lifters. Pill users who never met a clinician are a new, harder-to-retain segment.

insurance.state: Employer coverage recovered to 67% because oral-first step therapy cut the cost per member. About 90% of covering plans are gated and about half of those tenure-gated. Premium tiers keyed to verified kiosk weights are standard in the large benefits-administrator platforms. Pharmacy trend is ~+9%. Life insurers now ask about gray-market sourcing. Bone, fall and NAION costs land on Part A and Medicare Advantage.

pharma.state: Volume up ~30% over two years, with net price flat. Novo regains share with the 50 mg pill; Lilly leads on injectables and Foundayo. Both carry GI-MDL reserves in the low single-digit billions. Indian and Chinese makers dominate ex-US markets and the US gray market. Plaintiff-firm advertising for 'stomach paralysis' claims is a top-ten daytime TV category.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Income, still. Coached, trained bodies on injectable top-tier regimens read as top third, and the soft pill body reads as the middle. Visible cycling and regain read as gating, tenure gaps or parcel pens. A new signal is emerging: a deliberately unmedicated fuller body worn as a statement, most visibly among Black churchwomen 40–64 in Memphis and among young fat-liberation organisers in Portland.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use rates converge further, with the bottom third at 34.5% against 40% at the top, while body outcomes stay divergent. The pill brought the middle and lower-middle in without coaching. Lean-mass outcomes in that group look like those of the 2034 import users. That is the 'pill body', not the trained body.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: The Whole Table movement began in Memphis congregations in 2035 and now runs Sunday suppers in roughly 1,200 churches across the South and Midwest, with a no-scale, no-pill-at-table rule. Among the medicated, 'holiday weekends' and full-dose restarts on Monday are a normal rhythm.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list regimen, holiday schedule and sometimes 'Whole Table'. 'Unmedicated' is a larger niche than in 2034 and carries a political tint. Couples negotiate whose holidays line up.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Contested again. To the insured majority appetite is something to manage. A loud coalition calls it something God gave or the body knows: church groups, fat-acceptance revivalists, 'natural health' influencers and plaintiff-ad audiences. They are a minority, and the majority is still growing. Both sides cite the stomach-paralysis trials.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. ≈11M Americans are on top-dose triple or dual regimens; at 12% versus 5%, that implies ≈770k excess clinically meaningful anhedonia cases if the association is causal. The 2035 low-dose cohort suggests ~2 pts excess, which would mean on the order of 1.5–2M among ≈90M low and standard-dose users. Confounding is heavy. About 30% of users (≈31M) report at least one planned 'dose holiday' in the past year, and 'the grey' is the most-cited reason after social eating. 'Calm' and 'focus' subscribers fell to ≈4.1M.
interior_life.framing: Complaint, and only grudgingly a feature. 'The grey' is a talk-show and sitcom word. 'Quiet' and 'Even' rebranded around 'balance' and now market 'flex dosing' that builds in weekends off. Clinicians call it reward modulation; users say they're 'going colour for the weekend.'
interior_life.effect_on_work: Tenure-gated coverage keeps 'metabolic tenure' in place for warehouse and call-centre staff. White-collar 'focus' reimbursement continues but HR materials now mention holidays. Sales and hospitality staff take holidays before peaks instead of dosing down. Unions bargain over whether GI-related or holiday gaps count against adherence gates.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Grey era' is now a mocking label. Comedians do holiday-weekend material. Nashville and Memphis musicians tied to Whole Table record 'full-table gospel'. High-stimulus leisure keeps growing and peaks on weekends.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists build schedules around holidays. 'Colour weekends' are common, and so is Monday nausea. Couples counselling deals with mismatched holidays and with one partner joining Whole Table.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The 2036 presidential campaign treats price, the parked generic and sourcing as bipartisan grievances. Whole Table and 'natural' framings are courted by populist candidates, and plaintiff-bar money funds anti-pharma ads. No legislation moved and no government action followed.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding but static. It issued the survodutide MASH complete response letter and routine warning letters to telehealth fronts and exporters. It made no new label actions, prosecuted no individuals, and has no import or authentication law to enforce. FTC consent orders stand. The courts, not regulators, are where the action is: the generic-forfeiture injunction and the GI MDL.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Unchanged: Part D obesity benefit at $199/$50, and the 90% Medicaid match for 31 states plus DC on the continuation standard. No new state action and no mandate. The conditioning that spread this step is private: oral-first step therapy, tenure gates and kiosk-weight premium tiers.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged (≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weights, 5% response or override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+, 90-day bone pause, two misses means a 6-month suspension). Indiana and Arkansas keep 12-month rules. Privately, holidays now collide with the PDC-style adherence gates that employers copied from CMS. Pharmacy-claims refill gaps from planned holidays trigger gate warnings, so users shift holiday supply to cash $149 starters or gray product.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers to tirzepatide; fleets keep voluntary visual-field checks. Army accession is still contested, and Air Force waivers continue. No FMCSA rule.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API and Indian finished product still supply most of the 10.6M-user US gray market. Section 232 tariffs remain. The Telangana import alert is still an irritant in US–India talks. Mexican border pharmacies have become a large oral-semaglutide channel for Texas and Arizona.

events.event: The three largest PBMs adopt 'oral-first' step therapy for obesity coverage: members must try the 50 mg Wegovy pill or Foundayo for six months before an injectable is covered. Employer coverage ticks back up as per-member costs fall, and daily orals pass half of all US incretin use by year-end

The mid-2035 contingent date for rival generic semaglutide passes with no launch. The parked first filer sues FDA over a forfeiture decision on its 180-day exclusivity, and a D.C. federal judge enjoins approval of rival ANDAs pending appeal. Portal and list prices stay where they have been since 2033

First bellwether trial in the consolidated GLP-1 gastrointestinal litigation ends with a $4.2M jury verdict for a plaintiff with persistent gastroparesis on a failure-to-warn theory. Filed claims across federal and state dockets pass 70,000, and a second bellwether in March 2036 goes for the defence

A propensity-matched cohort of 38,000 low-dose oral users reports modestly higher anhedonia scores. Combined with a viral 'colour weekend' trend, a national poll finds three in ten users took a planned dose holiday that year, and 'Quiet' rebrands to 'flex dosing'

FDA warning letters to six telehealth 'peptide clinics' selling offshore-compounded retatrutide, survodutide and amycretin by subscription find most of them already reincorporated under new names. Gray and imported users reach an estimated 10.6M

About 40,000 people rally at the Whole Table convocation in Memphis. The movement, started in Black congregations in 2035, has drawn in fat-acceptance groups and 'natural health' influencers, and it now claims 1,200 churches holding no-scale, no-pill Sunday suppers

open_tensions: Generic semaglutide is enjoined pending a D.C. Circuit appeal on 180-day forfeiture. Prices have been flat since 2033, about 10.6M Americans buy gray or imported product, and offshore peptide clinics now sell molecules FDA has approved only as branded injectables. Congress has passed neither an import law nor an authentication law.

The GI MDL has over 70,000 claims, split bellwethers, and a pending general-causation ruling on pancreatic cancer. Holiday-and-restart dosing, which the culture now treats as normal, generates exactly the acute GI events plaintiffs cite, and no regulator has addressed it.

Private conditioning keeps spreading without government action: oral-first step therapy, tenure gates and kiosk-weight premiums. Adherence gates penalise the holidays most users now take, which pushes holiday supply into cash and gray channels.

Medicare holds the oldest users at a fixed $199. About 20,000 excess hip fractures and about 2,900 excess NAION cases a year are paid by Part A and Medicare Advantage and unscored, while the Whole Table bloc and plaintiff-bar money make the drug's politics a 2036 campaign theme with no policy attached.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
The permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 copay, eligibility BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, and the counselling visit.
The CMS continuation standard is unchanged, including the 90-day 'bone pause' code, and the same 31 states plus DC use it for the 90% Medicaid match.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.
The FTC consent orders still bar 'anxiety treatment' claims while permitting 'calm' and 'focus' marketing, and the 'Safe Pens' authentication bill remains stalled in Congress.

prose.headline: The Pill Won, the Generic Didn't Come, and Memphis Pulled Up a Chair: America at 37 Percent
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036, about three American adults in eight are on an incretin drug, and most of them now take it as a pill. The 50 mg Wegovy tablet approved in 2034 was never stronger than the weekly shot. It only matched it. That turned out to be enough once the big pharmacy-benefit managers decided, in the spring of 2035, that nobody would get an injectable covered until they had spent six months on a pill. Employers liked the arithmetic, and a few who had dropped coverage after the 2033 price rise came back. The needle is now something you graduate to if your plan lets you, and mostly the plans that let you are the ones attached to good jobs.

The price has not fallen. It has not risen either. It has simply stopped. The rival generics that were due in mid-2035 are held up behind an injunction while the first filer, whose plant is still under an import alert, argues in a Washington appeals court that it never forfeited the right to go first. The $149 starter doses on the federal portal are the cheapest legal door, and millions of people now take a starter dose indefinitely because it is what they can pay for. Medicare still pays $199 and charges $50, as the statute says. Almost nineteen million Medicare beneficiaries are on the drug, and the bones are paying for it somewhere else in the budget.

The people who cannot get through any door have not stopped either. There are about ten and a half million of them, buying Indian pens, Mexican border tablets, pressed counterfeits, and something new: subscriptions from telehealth 'peptide clinics' that ship offshore-compounded triple agonists in plain mailers and reincorporate every time the FDA sends a letter. Nobody has died in the numbers of November 2033, but the Florida and Texas abscess clusters come every few months.

The drug's own side effects are now a courtroom story. More than seventy thousand people have sued over stomachs that, they say, stopped working. A Philadelphia jury gave one of them $4.2 million last October, and a second jury in March gave another nothing. Daytime television runs ads asking whether your digestion was paralysed. The doctors' answer is diabetes, confounding, and a label that already warned. The lawyers' answer is the restarts. Three in ten users now take planned 'dose holidays' around weekends, weddings and Thanksgiving, sometimes to eat and sometimes to feel something. Many come back on Monday at full dose and spend Monday night in the emergency room.

The feeling is what changed most in public. In 2034 'calm' was a product. In 2036 'the grey' is a complaint you hear on sitcoms. A large observational study found low-dose users slightly more anhedonic than matched non-users. It proved nothing, and everyone had already decided. The calm brands now sell 'flex dosing' with the weekends built in.

Against all this a counter-movement has found a table. Whole Table began in Memphis congregations as Sunday suppers with no scale at the door and no pill at the plate. It now claims twelve hundred churches, a fat-liberation wing in Portland, natural-health influencers, and the quiet sympathy of plaintiff firms who buy airtime near its services. Forty thousand people came to Memphis in April. The movement is loud, real and a minority, and the number of people taking the drug rose nine points anyway.

No law passed. No agency changed a rule. Employers wrote the new conditions: tenure gates, kiosk weights, pill first. Every presidential candidate talks about the price, and nobody has a bill.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Saturday, Tanya Boyd does not take her Foundayo. She leaves the bottle on the windowsill above the sink, where she can see it and not touch it. By noon the chicken she is frying for tomorrow smells like chicken used to smell, and she eats a wing standing up and has to sit down from how good it is.

The plan from the school district covers Foundayo with a forty-dollar copay. The injectable is two years and a step-therapy form away. The district's kiosk is by the cafeteria freezer, and on the first of the month she weighs in where the kids can't see.

Sunday at Greater New Bethel the sign at the fellowship-hall door says WHOLE TABLE — LEAVE IT IN THE CAR. Her sister Renée has never taken anything and runs the serving line. Renée doesn't say a word about the windowsill. She doesn't have to.

Pastor talks about manna, about taking what is given. Tanya has seconds of greens and cobbler and laughs at something Deacon Pruitt says, really laughs, from her stomach.

At home her son is watching a ballgame. The ad comes on between innings: Did your weight-loss drug paralyse your stomach? A woman in a hospital gown. He looks at her and she looks at the screen.

Monday, five-forty, she takes the pill with coffee at the full dose, because the pharmacist's sheet about starting low again is somewhere in a drawer. By the second lunch period she is in the staff bathroom with her forehead on the cool metal of the stall. Then she goes back out and counts milk cartons.
